title: C programmers commit fresh crimes against readability
summary: The Register publishes an article highlighting common readability issues and poor coding practices found in C programs, discussing how C programmers often write code that prioritizes cleverness over clarity, making maintenance and understanding difficult for other developers.
problem_solved: Addresses the ongoing problem of unreadable, obfuscated C code that plagues codebases and makes collaboration difficult
why_valuable: Raises awareness about code quality standards and encourages developers to prioritize readability over clever one-liners in C programming
